hz6_state.topic: Hezbollah in Lebanese politics: elections, 2008 clashes and Doha, the Hariri tribunal, the port blast probe and Tayouneh, the 2019 protests

claims.text: Hezbollah won 8 of 128 seats in 1992 with 4 allied independents in its bloc; 7 in 1996; 10 in 2000; 14 in 2005; 13 in 2009, 2018 and 2022; joined cabinet for first time in 2005 (labour; energy and water), withdrew 2006, rejoined July 2008
2018: Hezbollah and allies won 71 seats; Nasrallah: 'Today I can say that our goals have been achieved'
May 2022: Hezbollah-led coalition won 61 of 128 seats, down about 10, losing its majority; Hezbollah and Amal kept all 27 Shia seats
9 March 2026: parliament voted 76 of 128 to extend its own mandate two years, postponing elections due in May 2026, a week after Hezbollah fired into Israel

The Conversation (Rebeiz) gives 12 seats in 1992 (counting the bloc); Arab Barometer early 2024: 30% of Lebanese trust Hezbollah, 55% not at all; 85% of Shia respondents, 9% Sunni and Druze, 6% Christian

Hezbollah-linked hospitals licensed by Islamic Health Authority; flagship al-Rasool al-Azam; Health Ministry under Diab added 15 Hezbollah-sponsored centres to state-funded list; state funding for Hezbollah-run hospitals rose from about 16bn to 30bn lira
Hamzeh (2004) reports Hezbollah served about 400,000 people with healthcare in 2000; Qassem (2005) says it repaired 17,212 homes damaged by Israeli raids 1991-2000 (Hezbollah's own figure)

6 May 2008 cabinet declared Hezbollah's telephone network illegal and removed Beirut airport security chief; Nasrallah 8 May called it 'a declaration of war'; Hezbollah controlled key areas 9-12 May and handed them to army; govt reversed both decisions 14 May; officials estimated 81 killed, 250+ injured by 12 May
Siniora 10 May 2008 called Hezbollah's actions an attempted coup; Doha agreement 21 May gave opposition 'effective veto'; Suleiman elected 25 May
Hezbollah gunmen knocked Future TV off the air and attacked an affiliated newspaper
2008 deaths: UN June 2008 report 69 killed and 180+ wounded; HRW at least 71; estimates range 70-110; Hezbollah said the network was part of its military apparatus
Doha: 30-minister cabinet 16 majority / 11 opposition / 3 president; parties agreed to ban weapons and violence in political disputes

STL 18 Aug 2020 convicted Salim Ayyash of the 14 Feb 2005 bombing that killed Hariri and 21 others and injured 226; acquitted Merhi, Oneissi, Sabra; no evidence implicating Hezbollah's leadership or direct evidence of Syria; Syria and Hezbollah 'may have had motives'; Hezbollah denied involvement; fifth accused's case dropped after he was killed in Syria in 2016

Appeals chamber March 2022 convicted Merhi and Oneissi; 16 June 2022 sentenced to life in absentia; Ayyash sentenced to life in 2020; Hezbollah refused to surrender them and Nasrallah refused to recognise the court; court cost estimated $600m-$1bn, 51% donors 49% Lebanon

July 2011 STL indicted four Hezbollah members; Nasrallah: they could not be arrested 'in 30 days or 60 days, or in a year, two years, 30 years or 300 years'; Hezbollah and allies resigned from government in 2011 over the tribunal
Port blast 4 Aug 2020 killed about 220; Hezbollah reportedly tried to quash investigation; Nasrallah denied responsibility
Wafiq Safa reportedly told judicial superiors on 20 Sept 2021 'should he drift off the course, we will remove him'; reported by Lebanese media
Bitar described the warning in a letter to the prosecutor and justice minister; Safa did not respond; Bitar had not sought to question Hezbollah members, only allied politicians
Nasrallah 11 Oct 2021: Bitar using 'the blood of the victims to serve political interests'; 'clearly political targeting'; called on Higher Judicial Council

Tayouneh 14 Oct 2021: Amal/Hezbollah protest against Bitar's warrant for Ali Hassan Khalil; seven killed (three Amal, three Hezbollah, one woman), about 30 injured; Amal and Hezbollah blamed Lebanese Forces, LF denied; Nasrallah 18 Oct accused LF of seeking civil war; no official findings published by Oct 2022
Probe stalled after Hezbollah accused Bitar of bias and officials filed lawsuits; Oueidat blocked resumption early 2023; Bitar resumed 16 Jan 2025 and charged 10
Bitar submitted his report late March 2026, reportedly accusing 70 people; no indictment as of 4 August 2026

Oct 2019 attacks on protesters: Nabatieh 23 Oct 400+ men identified by protesters as Hezbollah supporters; Beirut 29 Oct attackers chanting for Berri and Nasrallah burned tents in Martyrs' Square; no arrests; at least six security-force failures

hz6_money.topic: Hezbollah's funding, Syria intervention costs and US measures

claims.text: Nasrallah, speech of 24 June 2016: 'Hezbollah's budget, its income, its expenses, everything it eats and drinks, its weapons and rockets, come from the Islamic Republic of Iran'; 'As long as Iran has money, we have money'; 'We don't transfer our money through the Lebanese banking system'; responding to Hezbollah International Financing Prevention Act signed 18 Dec 2015
Speech marked 40 days after commander Mustafa Badreddine's death in Damascus
Ambassador Nathan Sales, 13 Nov 2018: Iran spends about $700m a year on Hezbollah, close to $1bn on militant groups, $100m to Palestinian groups; Iran said sanctions would not deter its support
State Department Country Reports on Terrorism 2018: Iran's support 'an estimated $700 million per year', 'the overwhelming majority of the group's annual budget'
Mandelker (June 2018): 'Iran provides upwards of $700 million a year to Hezbollah', against earlier US estimates of about $200m

2010 US estimate $100-200m/year; Iran reportedly cut funding 2009 and 2010; Feb 2012 Nasrallah acknowledged Iran's 'moral, and political and material support in all possible forms' since 1982 and denied US money-laundering and drug-smuggling allegations

Syria: Nasrallah first confirmed Hezbollah fighting in Syria 25 May 2013; 'Syria is the backbone of the resistance'; rebel control of border 'a great threat to Lebanon'; thousands of fighters by 2014; at least 1,300 killed by 2015; estimates 1,000-2,000 by 2018; key role in decisive battle Dec 2016

AP 2018: budget strained since entering Syria in 2013; estimated 2,000 fighters killed; cutting fighters in Syria; donation boxes; Sessions designated Hezbollah a top transnational organized crime threat 15 Oct 2018; Trump signed law expanding sanctions; State Dept: Iran spent $16bn since 2012 on Assad and proxies; Nasrallah: 'We have to tighten belts a bit' (reported), sanctions 'will have an effect for sure'

Rebeiz: Hezbollah sent thousands of fighters to help the Syrian government suppress the uprising; Iranian backing enabled a financial network involved in money laundering and drug trafficking (author's characterisation)

NOW 2022: maximum-pressure sanctions after 2018 cut the money Hezbollah received, forcing austerity; 2020 US refused aid to Health Ministry while Hezbollah ran it; Al-Qard al-Hassan described by researcher Yara Asmar as Hezbollah's alternative to the banking system

22 December 2016: Hezbollah helped the Syrian government win the battle for Aleppo (Reuters, via Wikipedia); 2010 US estimate of $100-200m a year; Dec 2010 reported 40% funding cut attributed to Israeli claims

State Department CRT 2018: Hezbollah's activity in Syria and Lebanon continued to pose a threat to Israel; Israeli concerns that Iran was helping Hezbollah build capacity to make rockets and missiles in Lebanon and Syria

hz6_syria.topic: Hezbollah's own acts in Syria: Qusayr 2013, Madaya/Zabadani 2015-17, UN COI and HRW findings, Assad's fall Dec 2024

claims.text: UN COI A/HRC/24/46 (16 Aug 2013, period 15 May-15 July 2013), Annex III: 'Pro-Government forces, including Hezbollah, launched a major offensive against the region of Al-Qusayr'; offensive 'supported by foreign combatants including thousands of Hezbollah fighters'; Hezbollah took control of Ain Tanour and Hamah water stations by early May; Hezbollah fighters controlled Sunni villages SW of Qusayr; Government forces and Hezbollah fighters took the town; rebels withdrew 5 June along a narrow corridor

UN COI A/HRC/24/46 para 173: government forces, backed by Hezbollah, intensified sieges in Homs before ground offensives, especially the May Qusayr offensive; para 179: government forces and Hezbollah conducted siege operations in violation of obligations under IHL (Chinese-language text, translated)
HRC resolution 23/1, 29 May 2013, 36-1-8: condemned 'the intervention of foreign combatants fighting on behalf of the Syrian regime in Al Qusayr' without naming any group

Qusayr fell 5 June 2013 after a 17-day battle; Hezbollah sent about 1,200 special forces to spearhead it (per a Hezbollah veteran); opposition sources said 70-110 Hezbollah fighters killed; Naim Qassem called it 'a sharp blow to the American-Israeli-Takfiri project'
Al Jazeera: Hezbollah fighters backed government forces; civilians trapped for weeks without water or electricity; siege of more than two weeks

Madaya besieged since July 2015 by Syrian army and Hezbollah (VOA; HRW citing residents: 'both government and allied Hezbollah forces'); MSF: 23 died of starvation at an MSF-supported centre after 1 Dec 2015 (HRW, 8 Jan 2016); 28 since 1 Dec (VOA); 16 more since the first aid convoy in January (MSF, 29 Jan 2016); about 20,000 people per MSF; MSF names the 'Syrian government-led coalition'
Hezbollah accused militants inside Madaya of 'withholding food from the locals'; Al-Manar called starvation images fabrications
UN COI chair Pinheiro (Jan 2016): siege tactics 'target the civilian population by subjecting them to starvation'; commission denounced starvation as a weapon by both sides
Foua and Kefraya besieged by armed groups incl. al-Nusra (about 12,500 people per UN)

Zabadani offensive by pro-government forces from July 2015; six-month truce for Zabadani, Foua, Kefraya agreed ~24 Sept 2015 between Ahrar al-Sham and Iran under UN sponsorship; SOHR: between rebels and pro-regime forces and Hezbollah
Four-towns evacuation April 2017; car bomb at Rashidin on 15 April killed at least 126, at least 109 evacuees incl. 68 children; no claim

COI Aleppo report A/HRC/34/64 (1 March 2017): pro-government ground forces 'composed mostly of Syrian and foreign militias' executed hors de combat fighters and perceived opposition supporters; does not name Hezbollah; armed groups shelled western Aleppo indiscriminately

Qassem, 14 Dec 2024: 'Hezbollah has lost the military supply route through Syria at this stage'; 'a detail in the resistance's work'; route could return or 'we could look for other ways'; anti-Assad fighters seized Iraq-Syria border 6 Dec; Damascus fell 8 Dec; Hezbollah sent officers to oversee withdrawal of its fighters

AP 14 Dec 2024: Assad's fall cut a vital weapons-smuggling route; Aron Lund: Iran could still smuggle some things but 'not even close' to previous scale; Firas Maksad: 'an entirely new reality'; Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah: changes 'will not weaken us'

hz6_money2.topic: US designations and cases on Hezbollah finance: FTO 1997, Al-Qard al-Hassan 2007/2021, Lebanese Canadian Bank 2011/2013, Project Cassandra dispute, Captagon

claims.text: Secretary of State Albright designated Hizballah ('Party of God', 'Islamic Jihad') a Foreign Terrorist Organization effective 8 October 1997; SDGT October 2001

Treasury designated Al-Qard al-Hassan 24 July 2007: 'Hizballah has used AQAH as a cover to manage its financial activity'; after Sept 2006 designations Hizballah moved part of its financial activity to AQAH

11 May 2021 Treasury designated seven: Ibrahim Ali Daher (chief, Central Finance Unit) and six AQAH officials; AQAH an NGO licensed by the Interior Ministry providing bank-like services without licence; officials' accounts moved over $500 million through Lebanon's formal financial system over a decade; Gacki quote

10 Feb 2011 FinCEN/Treasury 311 finding: LCB a 'primary money laundering concern'; Ayman Joumaa network laundered up to $200m/month through LCB; US government information indicates Hizballah derived financial support from the network; LCB had 35 branches, assets over $5bn

SDNY 25 June 2013: LCB agreed to forfeit $102m of $150m seized Aug 2012; complaint alleged at least $329m wired to US 2007-2011 to buy used cars for West Africa, proceeds moved through Hizballah-controlled laundering channels; release does not say LCB admitted wrongdoing

Politico (Josh Meyer, December 2017): DEA's Project Cassandra, launched 2008, believed Hezbollah collected about $1bn a year from drugs/weapons; alleged Obama administration let Hezbollah 'off the hook' to secure Iran deal; Kevin Lewis: 'There has been a consistent pattern of actions taken against Hezbollah'; Derek Maltz pointed to turf battles

Byman (Lawfare): sourcing one-sided, relying on DEA; evidence stronger on interagency rivalry than White House pressure; Daniel Benjamin: 'woefully one-sided recitation from DEA'; Brian O'Toole: 'classic analytic overreach'

Treasury 28 March 2023: Maher al-Assad and the Fourth Division facilitate Captagon production and trafficking; al-Assad family dominates the trade; Hassan Daqqou linked to Fourth Division operations 'with cover reportedly provided by Hizballah'; Noah Zaitar 'close ties to both the SAA's Fourth Division and certain members of Hizballah'

OCCRP/BBC 2023: Lebanese records link Daqqou to the Fourth Division; Daqqou told investigators he worked with Hezbollah and travelled in its convoys; Lebanese judge found no evidence implicating Syrian officials; Hezbollah has denied any role; many Lebanese officials reluctant to tie Hezbollah directly
OCCRP 2020: Salerno seizure over 14 tonnes linked by Der Spiegel to Assad family network (Samer Kamal al-Assad factory)

New Lines (Shaar and Rose, May 2023): regime 'the main supplier and sponsor of the industry'; refers to 'regime- and Hezbollah-aligned individuals' without naming Hezbollah actors; New Lines and Der Spiegel estimated at least $5.7bn in 2021
Nasrallah, May 2023: reports 'baseless lies'; Captagon 'religiously prohibited'

WSJ Jan 2025: after Assad's fall rebels showed production sites in government air bases; US, European, Arab officials say Fourth Division oversaw most production; US and Arab officials say Hezbollah 'facilitated trafficking in areas under their control'; its profits from Captagon unknown
